fixes.rationale_full: The tests no longer read SSLSocket.isClosed(), which the JDK sets by itself when a read fails. RecordingSslSockets wraps every SSLSocket the real factory layers in RecordingSocket, a delegating SSLSocket (shape of ProxyTlsTest's DelegatingSocket, no mocking framework) that records each close() call with its thread and whether the plain socket under it was already closed, then delegates. assertAllClosed now requires, within 5 s, at least one recorded close() per created SSLSocket, every call made after the plain socket's close (A-001 order), and the real socket closed. The cross-thread abort test additionally asserts no close() was recorded before the abort and none ran on the thread that called res.abort; abortMillis < 1000 and endMillis < 2500 stay. New test sec_PROXY_005_anAbortBeforeTheCopyStartsClosesTheSslSocket: a middleware aborts after next.run() returned (res.relay has the body, the copy not started) and the SSLSocket must still get its close(). An abort-before-relay test (listener at registration) was tried and dropped: an aborted response never reaches the proxy (the dispatcher stops it), and the window between res.status and res.onAbort cannot be hit deterministically without a seam.

fixes.rationale_full: Verified against the code before relying on the guidance: DefaultResponse.abort snapshots copying under the response lock and calls closeInput only when no copy runs, then the listeners; runTransfer sets copying under the same lock and its finally always runs closeInput; startBody's refusal and Response.relay's default close the given stream; RelayedBodyStream.close runs super.close (SocketBodyStream.close -> BackendClient.closeConnection(plain, ssl)) before exchange.release, independent of the released flag. So from res.relay on the relayed body's close always closes the SSLSocket, on the copy thread after its read returned or with no reader active. Change: ProxyExchange.release(boolean closeTls) keeps the exactly-once sequence (released CAS, reservation cancel, close, limiter.release in nested finallys); release() = full close (forward's finally, RelayedBodyStream.close; attach-after-release unchanged) and the new package-private releaseOnAbortThread() closes only the recorded plain socket (or the attached socket when none was recorded), never the SSLSocket. Proxy's onAbort listener now calls releaseOnAbortThread after abandon(). Properties kept: A-001 (plain closed first everywhere; the recorded close calls assert it), R2-001 (every created SSLSocket still gets close(), asserted by all six SSLSocket tests). Javadoc claims that became false were replaced in ProxyExchange.release, Proxy.releaseOnAbort and BackendClient.closeConnection; TlsConnector and RelayedBodyStream comments stay accurate and were not changed. Residual: path (c) (abort between res.status and res.onAbort registration) relies on startBody's refusal closing the stream, verified by code reading only; the Conscrypt timing itself is not run (no Android runtime, device verification out of scope). No public symbol or signature changed.
